text:
Maria Gomez: Quick sync — I'm starting a controlled canary for a header-based SDK feature gate named `smart_cache` that changes caching semantics. Plan: enable for clients >= 2.5 on web (10%) and mobile (1%) for 48h, then widen if no regressions. Need owners for web SDK, mobile SDK, backend fallback, QA, and SRE guardrails.

Maria Gomez: Header format we'll use: `X-Redwood-Feature: smart_cache=on;sdk=2.5` — servers will only honor when `sdk` >= 2.5. Example curl:```bash
curl -H "X-Redwood-Feature: smart_cache=on;sdk=2.5" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Samir Patel: quick q — how do we behave for older clients that send no header? fallback to current (off) behavior?

Maria Gomez: yep. default is OFF. we will not change logic for clients without header. goal is opt-in via header only.

Samir Patel: ok. can you add server-side guard: if header sdk version looks malformed, treat as <=2.4 and log event `feature.header_malformed`?

Maria Gomez: good call — will add that and emit `feature.smart_cache.requested` + `feature.smart_cache.applied|denied`. I'll put event names in the rollout doc.

Priya Desai: QA heads up — I need a small test matrix: web 2.5rc + mobile 2.5rc + server fallback cases + malformed header. Can you post expected responses and a checklist?

Maria Gomez: on it. minimal checks: 1) header present + sdk>=2.5 => response includes `x-redwood-cache: hit|miss` header and <=200ms p50 change; 2) header present + sdk<2.5 => no cache header, behavior unchanged; 3) malformed header => 400-ish telemetry but normal response; 4) rate-limit/timeout fallout.

Julia Kim: web SDK will add header injection in 2.5.0-rc1. We can gate the injection behind a runtime flag so customers can opt out. We'll push a PR today — ping @maria for review. Also will submit a tiny shim to add header for older clients if they opt-in via config.

Leo Zhang: mobile release cadence slower — playbook: remote-config-driven rollout is easier for us than shipping the header in version X. can we support both? e.g., server-side allowlist by device id for mobile canary?

Maria Gomez: yes — mobile canary via allowlist is fine. we should set mobile to 1% by default. please add the allowlist id(s) to the rollout doc.

SRE Oncall: from SRE side we need: 1) kill switch API (already exists? if not, make one), 2) alerts on increased error rate, p95 latency by route, and cache-miss ratio change. recommend thresholds: error rate +0.5% absolute OR p95 +200ms OR cache-miss ratio +15% => page.

Maria Gomez: kill switch endpoint exists: `POST /admin/feature/kill/smart_cache` — will wire runbooks and add automation in the console to flip to 0% traffic for the flag. adding alerts to the rollout doc.

Samir Patel: backwards-compat check: ensure proxies and gateways don't strip `X-Redwood-Feature`. We had one issue last time. Please add a quick smoke that asserts header passes through edge.

Maria Gomez: noted. adding `edge.header_pass_through` smoke job.

Priya Desai: can we get a Canary dashboard view for the 48h window? need: % of traffic with header, errors by client version, `feature.smart_cache.applied` rate, and latencies.

Maria Gomez: will create a Grafana panel set and share link in the doc.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: smart_cache — web 10% (sdk>=2.5), mobile 1% (allowlist) — start=2026-03-20T17:00:00Z duration=48h

Julia Kim: PR #4212 ready, adds header injection + opt-out flag. linking in the rollout doc. :eyes:

Leo Zhang: I'll add mobile allowlist ids and remote-config toggle this afternoon. :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: assign me for server review — I'll check malformed parsing and telemetry hooks.

Maria Gomez: thanks all — tagging owners in the rollout doc for signoff. I'll start the canary once SRE confirms alerting and QA signs off. :rocket:
